112972154.title: File:Gas boiler hall in Iru Thermal Power Plant.jpg

ObjectName.value: Gas boiler hall in Iru Thermal Power Plant

Categories.value: 360° panoramas|Self-published work|Large images|Photographs by Lauri Veerde|360° panoramas of Iru power plant

ImageDescription.value: Energy production starts from boilers. On the right, there are 2 giant 34-meter-high gas boilers, each capable of producing up to 500 tons of steam per hour at the pressure of 14 MPa and at the temperature of 555 C. It would take less than a minute for this giant to heat the ice-cold water of a classic 4-row swimming pool to a comfortable 28 degrees. The hot steam generated in the boilers travels to the turbine hall next to it for the production of electricity. On the left, there are 3 smaller water heating boilers. These directly heat the water circulating in central heating networks. In the foreground, 4 giant network water heaters stand out, where the supply of heating water is kept. The free space at floor level is used as a workshop for the repair and maintenance of large equipment. The grab cranes of the waste bunker are also repaired here.
